A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Andrews–Curtis case study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching material relocated during the substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original search and PPO experiments, Transformer training and embedding results, and computations of presentation neighborhoods and persistent homology.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and reports additional variable-horizon PPO outcomes, computational trivializations, and quantitative feature-prediction experiments.

M1.justification: v2 adds staged-horizon PPO training and barcode features for hardness prediction. The underlying greedy-search rule, PPO objectives, reward function and networks, Transformer architecture, and adaptive-supermove Algorithm 3 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix B adds a tested presentation from the Meier–Zupan family, P(5, 2; 4/5), beyond the earlier Miller–Schupp and Akbulut–Kirby examples. The main 1,190-presentation dataset and approximately 1.8-million-presentation Transformer corpus remain unchanged; the newly solved Miller–Schupp cases belong to retained coverage.

E2.justification: The main BFS, greedy-search, and PPO comparisons remain. Section 8.2 adds explicit XGBoost comparisons using length-only and neighborhood-size baselines against barcode and combined features. The separate GS-versus-BFS comparison for the length-25 presentation in v1 Section 3.5 is omitted.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include PPO training for 100 million interactions with horizons increasing from 200 to 400, 800, and 1200, a 20-million-node greedy search on AK(5), and a 4:1 train/test split evaluated with F1 for the barcode-feature study. The original benchmark settings and Appendix A hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: v1 mainly reports neighborhood-size distributions and brief observations about centrality and spectral features. v2 adds barcode-vector sensitivity analysis, exhaustive feature-subset comparisons, and SHAP feature attribution in Section 8.2 and Figures 21–22. Section 7 also adds analysis of ratios between the retained AC and AC-prime graph statistics.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same five-seed experiment, individual solution counts, and mean of 334.4. v2 introduces no additional quantified uncertainty, confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run counts for its added experiments.

E6.justification: Under the new horizon schedule, v2 reports two additional Miller–Schupp solutions with shortened paths of 195 and 381 moves, plus a 49-move solution for P(5, 2; 4/5). New classifier F1 scores are 0.885 for length, 0.930 for neighborhood size, 0.943 for barcode features, and 0.962 for selected combined features. The principal fixed-setting search/PPO totals and Transformer validation loss remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v1's Theorem 1 asserting stable AC-triviality of AK(3) is withdrawn after identifying its faulty premise. v2 adds proofs for infinite Miller–Schupp subfamilies, Akbulut–Kirby length reductions, and unknot-derived presentations, together with new conjectures and the Reidemeister-move proof in Appendix E. It also substantially expands the persistent-homology formalization.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace the claimed resolution of stable AC-triviality for AK(3) with length reduction for AK(n), n at least 5, and triviality results for three infinite Miller–Schupp subfamilies. They also foreground a global topological hardness measure and PPO successes on cases missed by greedy search.

C2.justification: The retained 53-move connection to AK(3) is explicitly reinterpreted as insufficient to establish stable AC-triviality. v2 adds explanations of the horizon curriculum, interprets barcode ratios as suggesting comparable complexity under different move sets, and distinguishes proven knot-presentation subclasses from broader unresolved conjectures.

D1.justification: v2 supplies additional explicit AC paths, identifies XGBoost and SHAP, and directs readers to a verification notebook. Existing hyperparameters and dataset-generation pseudocode are retained, while the giotto-TDA version and old AK(3) search-budget details are omitted. New printed paths use undefined h0 despite definitions running from h1 to h12, limiting reproducibility.

R1.justification: The relationship to Myasnikov–Myasnikov–Shpilrain changes fundamentally: a result previously used to justify the central theorem is scrutinized and its misprint shown to invalidate that application. v2 also positions its infinite-family results against Lisitsa's finite cases and adds connections to theorem-proving, learned optimization, and Meier–Zupan presentations.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution narrative, and outline are substantially rewritten. Language modeling moves ahead of topology; the former combined topology section becomes separate global-hardness and local-analysis sections; stable AC material is extensively rewritten in Section 9 and appendices. PPO discussion is reorganized into fixed- and variable-horizon subsections.

P2.justification: v2 adds RL and adaptive-action diagrams, feature-analysis plots, crossing and unknot diagrams, and Reidemeister illustrations. Existing comparison plots are relocated and rearranged. The graph-statistics tables are shortened to lengths 11–16 and supplemented by a ratio table; many retained plots preserve their underlying data.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves a central correctness problem by withdrawing v1's unsupported stable AC-triviality theorem for AK(3) and explaining the faulty premise in Appendix F. New mathematical proofs and quantitative hardness analyses substantially strengthen the paper. Undefined h0 entries in the new certificates remain a reproducibility defect, but the correction of the centerpiece claim and added supporting evidence provide a substantial net improvement.
